subject: general
question: Sapna invested ₹20,300 on simple interest, partly at 11% per annum and partly at 3% per annum. If she earns equal interests from the two investments after 5 years, then find the sum invested at 11% per annum (in ₹).
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When simple interests are equal for the same time period, the principal ratio is inversely proportional to the rate ratio.

Ratio of investments P₁ : P₂ = R₂ : R₁ = 3 : 11

Sum of ratio parts = 3 + 11 = 14 units

Sum invested at 11% (P₁) = (3 ÷ 14) × 20,300 = 3 × 1,450 = 4,350

**∴ The correct answer is ₹4,350.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total amount invested = ₹20,300

Rate 1 (R₁) = 11% per annum

Rate 2 (R₂) = 3% per annum

Time (T) = 5 years for both investments

Simple Interest from part 1 = Simple Interest from part 2

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100
